rubrics.justification: The response overcalls the image as a good expanded blastocyst with clear blastocoel, distinct ICM, and cohesive TE. In the image, expansion appears limited/uncertain, ICM is not clearly identifiable, and TE is not well visualized as a uniform epithelial layer. The suggested 4BB/4AB grade is not well supported.

It integrates most relevant factors well, including young age, ovarian reserve, prior live birth/miscarriage, BMI, smoking, endometrium, and sperm data, and relates them to prognosis. Some links are somewhat generic and the male-factor interpretation is speculative.

The structure is logical overall, but the prognosis is built partly on an overly optimistic morphology assessment. The implantation estimate is therefore only partially supported, and some statements (e.g., strong emphasis on smoking reducing rates by 10-20% in this exact case) are broader than the evidence provided.

Much of the counseling is reasonable and guideline-consistent, especially smoking cessation and general transfer support. However, recommending assisted hatching and strongly advocating PGT-A in a 28-year-old primarily due to one miscarriage are not clearly guideline-based for routine use.

The response gives clear practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including lifestyle counseling and possible further evaluation if failures recur. Some recommendations are useful but a few are not sufficiently individualized or may be premature.
